feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader: the experience progression is clear, the scope is substantial, and the public-sector specialization comes through well. It is well written overall, but it feels slightly dense and repetitive, and it would be stronger with sharper outcomes and tighter section consolidation.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression at NACo strongly support leadership credibility.  
- Good evidence of scale and complexity: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, analytics stack, and studio build-out add impact.  
- Writing is polished and professional, with no obvious misspellings; tone is consistent and appropriate for strategic digital leadership roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidating them would improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond activity descriptions, especially in the freelance role and earlier positions (e.g., growth, efficiency gains, engagement lifts, cost savings).  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; bullet punctuation and dash formatting are inconsistent; “French (A2/Learning)” reads awkwardly—use “French (A2, learning)” or “Elementary.”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and public-sector positioning. It’s slightly dense and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent NACo experience, so tightening it will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “Senior digital leader” with a more specific positioning tied to enterprise/public-sector digital transformation.
- Add 1–2 concrete scale signals from recent work to increase credibility.
- Tighten the service list so it reads as a focused value proposition, not a duplicate skills summary.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web, analytics, and editorial systems for high-volume public-sector organizations. Leads digital governance, CMS and workflow improvement, multimedia operations, and AI-enabled content experiences that strengthen discovery, publishing efficiency, and audience engagement.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” repeats the subtitle’s leadership framing.
- The long list of capabilities overlaps with Core Competencies and Topline Skills; keep the intro higher-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the headline and recent roles, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize strategic capability areas rather than repeating detailed skill phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use broader, executive-level categories to reduce repetition and improve scanability.
- Prioritize the most recent/high-value strengths: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI/search, and cross-channel operations.
- Standardize phrasing for parallel structure; avoid mixing systems, functions, and outputs in one list.
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and performance insights • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” repeats the header and Recent Projects almost verbatim.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” and analytics/governance items are already covered in Topline Skills and Technical + IT.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant examples that reinforce your current positioning, but the block is too dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening the phrasing and making the format more scannable will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add bullets and parallel structure: “Project name: action + scope + outcome/purpose.”
- Tighten wording and remove filler: e.g., “bill-level AI chat” is strong; “designed for continued campaign growth” can become “built for reuse and expansion.”
- Standardize style and hyphenation: use “AI-enabled,” “bill-level,” and spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency.
- Consider this rewrite:  
  **Recent Projects**  
  • **AI Hybrid Search:** Built an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat.  
  • **We Are Counties Microsite:** Developed a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, and downloadable resources.  
  • **Organization Anniversary Campaign:** Produced a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10-by-20-foot interactive conference display.  
  • **Advocacy Video Series:** Launched a recurring advocacy video program spanning planning, production, and distribution across web, email, and social.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI search, microsites, and advocacy video work already appear in recent roles; keep this block concise to avoid repeating full responsibility statements.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Website

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a service list rather than a high-impact recent position. Tighten it around ownership, scope, and outcomes, and avoid repeating project details already covered in Recent Projects.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Serve as strategic communications and digital platforms consultant to a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign infrastructure, content operations, and AI-enabled search.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership verbs: led, built, redesigned, implemented, established, improved.
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-focused bullets, e.g.:
- Built digital workflows, analytics, and governance systems to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Developed Drupal campaign experiences, including scalable microsite architecture, modular content components, and member-facing resource hubs.
- Delivered front-end/CMS implementation and troubleshooting for high-traffic public web properties.
- Led AI-enabled search strategy spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user discovery.
- Add metrics if possible: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaign launches, time saved, engagement gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording overlaps with Recent Projects; keep this entry focused on role-level scope, not named project examples.
- “Governance/usability/best practices” repeats themes from the NACo role; emphasize what is new or more advanced here.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management for a high-volume public-sector communications operation.”
- Make the website bullet the anchor achievement: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Strengthen results language in other bullets: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing internal capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring video content.”
- Combine/trim channel and analytics bullets unless you can add performance gains: list audience size, engagement growth, reporting adoption, time saved, or decision-making improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version higher-level and more strategic.
- Video-programming language also echoes prior NACo roles; emphasize building the studio and scaling capacity, not routine production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the earlier NACo role and the later Director role. Make it more clearly about operating ownership, editorial coordination, and channel growth at this mid-level stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and progression: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and start with outcomes/action: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video contribution: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger line: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” repeat themes covered in the Director role; keep this version more execution-focused.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/owning the program, not launching it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/freelance experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and avoid generic phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive bullets:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance, publishing standards, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social, and video
- Audience-centered messaging for advocacy and member engagement
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for “Content operations and governance” if you want stronger alignment with recent leadership roles.
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve measurable scale (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) for experience bullets rather than skills.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” repeat language already used in the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill mix, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent execution strengths rather than repeat a software inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters tied to recent work: “Drupal platform delivery • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Drop lower-priority or older-signal items here, especially “jQuery,” unless central to target roles.
- Consider replacing “WordPress - SharePoint - Power Pages” with “Multi-CMS administration (Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages)” to reduce listiness.
- If space allows, add one impact cue: “Drupal modernization for large public-facing sites” or “enterprise web platforms and integrations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Web Platforms & CMS” and “Coding & Technical Implementation.”
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also repeats Core Competencies and recent project content.

items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:

- Executive and leadership reporting dashboards

- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so this item should emphasize execution depth or leadership use cases.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and older NACo bullets. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production capability and recent relevance rather than listing basic tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Operations**

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Use this line to signal depth in the most relevant CMSs—especially Drupal—rather than repeat names only.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize level of use: “Drupal (enterprise architecture, migration, modular content) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add recency/strength ordering: put Drupal first and consider dropping GitHub Pages if it’s minor relative to enterprise platforms.
- Consider a sharper title: “CMS Platforms” or “Web Platforms (Enterprise CMS)” for concision.
- If truthful, add version/scope detail for impact: e.g., “Drupal 10” or “SharePoint Online.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- “CMS modernization” is already covered elsewhere, so don’t repeat that phrase here unless replacing a weaker platform entry.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this item reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools not already captured elsewhere and modernize the phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS, JavaScript, API integrations, GTM, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) and consider removing jQuery unless it is still actively used in recent work.
- Group by function for readability: Front-end: HTML, CSS, JavaScript | Integrations: APIs, Google Tag Manager | Deployment/automation: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- If possible, add scope in another section rather than here, e.g., “used for Drupal front-end implementation, tagging, lightweight edge scripts, and deployment workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- GitHub Actions may fit better under “Automation & Workflow Systems” if you want this item focused purely on coding stack.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Workflow automation / Airtable systems” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize systems actually used to build automation and coordination workflows.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Reorder by relevance/strength: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Trello • Basecamp
- If accurate, add light qualifiers instead of a bare list: Airtable (workflow databases) • Power Automate/Zapier (process automation) • Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp (project tracking) • Slack/Teams (cross-team coordination)
- If space is tight, cut 1–2 lower-value/general collaboration tools and keep the strongest automation signals first.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack and Teams are common workplace tools; keep them only if they were central to operational systems, not just everyday communication.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory. Tie it more clearly to email operations/marketing automation and keep it aligned with the stronger evidence already shown in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform names for readability: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers instead of just tools, e.g. “newsletter operations, audience segmentation, journey automation” in a short parenthetical or fold into a summary skills line elsewhere.
- Order by strongest/recent relevance; if Dynamics 365 was only light exposure, lead with Higher Logic/Mailchimp instead.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters and multi-channel communications; avoid repeating outcomes here.
- “Engagement” is broad and may duplicate Core Competencies; keep this item tool-specific.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is mostly a keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Tighten it to emphasize analytics infrastructure and optimization methods rather than repeating generic terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • KPI design • SEO/performance analysis • Experimentation
- Replace “A/B testing” with “Experimentation” if formal testing was limited; it sounds broader and more credible.
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “KPI design” or “Executive reporting” to better reflect strategic ownership and match your Director-level experience.
- Order by strongest, most recent tools first: GA4, Clarity, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly duplicated by “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Consider keeping the detailed version in one place only.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already substantiated in the 2022–2024 NACo role, so avoid repeating too many generic labels elsewhere.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads like a setup for later NACo roles rather than a distinct accomplishment entry. Tighten it around team-building, platform work, and content production with any available scale.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and improve workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Split key contributions into concrete outcomes: website refresh, livestream/video production, and informal supervision/coordination.
- Add metrics if available: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social volume supported, or efficiency gains from workflow improvements.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported a major website refresh, improved cross-channel publishing workflows, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this version focused on launching/building the format, not scaling it.
- Avoid repeating broad “web, email, social, video” leadership language already covered more strongly in later roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia and innovation work, but it reads broadly and undersells impact. Since later NACo roles already cover digital leadership, keep this focused on foundational project coordination and the podcast launch.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and “firsts”: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Tighten the second sentence and foreground the strongest achievement: “Produced digital and multimedia content, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If possible, add outcomes: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audience/downloads, or teams/stakeholders coordinated.
- Consider a two-bullet format for clarity rather than one paragraph.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating generic “digital content production” language already covered in later NACo roles; make this item distinctly about innovation/research support and the first podcast launch.
- Don’t overstate video/multimedia leadership here if those accomplishments are stronger and more recent in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so tighten it to tool proficiency only.

Suggested edit:
